items.english: Let it be said in passing that Liu was not, by nature, a man who delighted in visitors. But when he already had one guest with him, and a new visitor came, he would generally receive him readily enough. He had what might be called a childish vanity, as if to boast before his guest of having guests. Besides, today's barbarian monk was just now talked of wherever one went. By no means a visitor to be ashamed of meeting. — Liu's motive in proposing to meet him lay much in this direction.

notes: The text names no speaker for p15-p16; the two lines are exchanged between Liu and Sun Sensei, with the second, dismissive surmise most likely Sun Sensei's. I have left the attribution unstated as in the Japanese.

items.english: "Begging, most likely. He will be asking us to bestow some alms, I suppose."

While the two were talking such matters over, presently there entered, led by the maid, as they looked, a strange-formed monk, tall and with eyes like cut amethysts. He wore a yellow robe, his grown-out curling hair hanging heavily, as if a nuisance, over his shoulders. Fly-whisk with its red handle in hand, he planted himself heavily in the middle of the room. He offered no greeting and said not a word.
notes: For the eyes, shisekiryou, I have used cut amethysts for the purple faceted stone; the exact mineral is uncertain.

items.english: Liu hung back for a while, but as the silence grew somehow uneasy, he ventured, "Have you some business with me?"
At which the barbarian monk said, "You are the one, are you not, who is fond of drink."

"Indeed." The question came so abruptly that Liu gave a vague answer, looking toward Sun Sensei as if seeking rescue. Sun Sensei, with a composed face, went on placing stones on the board by himself. He showed no disposition whatever to take part.

"You are afflicted with a rare disease. Are you aware of it?" The barbarian monk said this as if to press the point. Hearing of a disease, Liu wore a dubious look, stroking the bamboo wife as he did so—
notes: Bamboo wife kept as in the bible: the jointed rattan bolster leaned on in summer heat; the sentence trails in the Japanese into Liu's reply in p22.
